dimension: TRACK A, USE AN APP (benchmark sections 1 and 2): choose an app -> install or open -> run an example -> save results
already_met: Two-track structure and a beginner skeleton exist. /use/ (docs/use/index.md, from data/hubs.yaml) shows three cards in task order: 'Install it' -> 'Open it and work' -> 'Use it in your image software (soon)'. The same docs sidebar (Install and open: Install an app, Open and use an app, Use notebooks after installation, Troubleshooting an installed app) appears on every guide page (seen in screenshots).

App page lands on installation, not on the Docs homepage. /apps/nucleisky/ has OS tiles with a 'YOUR SYSTEM' marker and short hints (Windows: 'choose More info, then Run anyway'; macOS: 'Apple menu, About This Mac: Intel, or M1 and later'; Linux: 'Run it with: bash <file name>'), then 'Need help installing? See the install guide' and a 'How to install' section. Both links are href='../../guides/install/' in site/apps/nucleisky/index.html.

install.md uses real dialog and menu labels, in ordered steps per OS: 'Windows protected your PC' > 'More info' > 'Run anyway'; macOS About This Mac > System Settings > Privacy & Security > 'Open Anyway' (with the note that it appears only after a first attempt); Linux `bash <file>`. It has an alt-texted screenshot, an honest 6-8 minute estimate, and a 'Check where it comes from' notice that says the installers are unsigned. The built page equals origin/main's .tools/docs/install.md apart from link rewrites (I diffed them).

Search for the Windows warning works. Typing 'Windows protected your PC' in the site search returns 'Install an app > Windows' as the only and first hit. 'how to run a notebook' returns 'Use notebooks after installation > 3. How to Run Notebooks?' first (I tested both in the browser against /search.json).

The Use hub has an immediate failure route: the orange 'Something went wrong? ... Troubleshooting an installed app' callout on /use/. The hand-written content/guides/using-apps.md also ends with a 'Something went wrong' section that links to the install guide, the troubleshooting guide and the app's 'Report a problem'.

Single-source editing and link integrity hold. The edit links of the four Use guides point to the true sources: LabConstrictor .tools/docs/install.md, notebook_usage.md and troubleshooting_installed_app.md, and LabConstrictor-Site content/guides/using-apps.md. I ran scripts/check_site.py and scripts/check_design.py: '38 pages, 0 problems' each.

The App Centre already has the hooks for an app-owned example. labconstrictor-app.schema.json defines an optional `quickstart` (up to 6 plain-text steps) and `docs_url`. pages_apps.using_section renders both, so the missing piece is app content, not site machinery.

gaps.requirement: Benchmark s4 and s7 'Scientific examples': every featured scientific app has at least one reproducible example (small downloadable data, parameters, expected output, limitations), owned by the app repository and linked from the App Centre.
gaps.current: None of the 6 manifests in build/snapshot.json sets `quickstart`, and none sets `docs_url` (VLab4Mic only has `homepage`). So every app page prints the same generic 'Using it' paragraph plus 'Read more: README on GitHub' (docs/apps/nucleisky/index.md). NucleiSky is featured and has no example: every notebook asks for your own files (2DApp 'Full Path' placeholder '/path/to/large_image.tif'; NucleiSky2D_API_Workflow_Example cell 3 `base_path = Path("path/to/your/data")`). `git ls-files` shows only banners and logos, no images. The README promises 'align your images in minutes' without a data link, and its docs are Python-API oriented. README links 'desktop installer' to .tools/docs/download_executable.md, whose download URLs point to CellMigrationLab/NucleiSky-test/releases/... (lines 13, 51, 111, 117, 152, 158), not NucleiSky. The Welcome table lists six notebooks with no 'start here', and the API example's description is a copy of the App's ('This notebook 'NucleiSky2DApp.ipynb' is for running NucleiSky2D as an App'). CellTracksColab is the one app with a real example: each notebook has a 'Use test dataset' checkbox that downloads Zenodo record 8413510 (T_cell_dataset.zip, 'up to 10 min download'), a 'Results folder:' box, and outputs such as Tracks/, QC/ and merged_Tracks.csv.gz. Its README Quick Start Option B describes the desktop route, but never says what the result looks like. The site does not surface it. GuessTheCondition needs your own folder tree of TIFFs; the Demo app needs an uploaded image; VLab4Mic's README defers to an external website. The Playground ('Check everything' -> readout + report.json) is the only zero-data run with a defined output, and it is listed under 'Testing and maintenance'. All six apps have tier 'listed', none verified.
